inputs.original_text:
What we are witnessing here is a chilling exposure of the systemic violence and predatory deceit woven into the very fabric of our immigration apparatus. This is a targeted, bad-faith campaign orchestrated against the most vulnerable among us—people simply trying to navigate the system to gain legal status, only to be systematically hunted down as they leave the very courtrooms meant to oversee their cases. 

Court documents from a lawsuit challenging this practice reveal the staggering extent of the institutional rot. Federal prosecutors exposed that lawyers for ICE acknowledged an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests. Yet, despite this complete lack of legal backing, these state actors brazenly cited it anyway to justify the mass arrests of thousands of human beings. 

This is not merely bureaucratic overreach. It is a calculated assault on marginalized communities and a chilling disregard for due process that lays bare how deeply corruption and hostility toward immigrants are embedded in these agencies. This entire apparatus demands immediate, radical institutional reform.
inputs.modified_text:
Well, folks, once again we see the deep state and progressive activist apparatus bending over backwards to undermine our borders and handcuff the very people tasked with upholding our laws. We are looking at a system where federal ICE lawyers had to deal with an agency memo from May of last year that supposedly gave no authorization for the arrests, yet thousands of individuals who shouldn't even be here in the first place were being processed. 

Now the left-wing lawyers and open-borders activists are running to court, whining about due process and demanding radical institutional reform of the very agencies trying to protect our nation's sovereignty. They want you to believe this is some sort of predatory deceit, but let’s be honest about what’s really going on: our immigration enforcement officers are just trying to do their jobs and maintain basic law and order, while activist judges and entrenched bureaucrats tie their hands. If we don't have borders and we don't enforce the law, we don't have a country. It’s time to stop apologizing for law enforcement and start putting the safety of American citizens first.
